text:
amy: FYI - Bayleaf's onboarding health shows tail latency on their critical route /v1/complete. Renewal check in 10 days. Need a short evidence bundle + provisional credit calc.
lee: drop the SLOs and the last-7d numbers? will scope infra asks.
amy: SLA: 99.9% uptime. SLO (latency): 95% of requests < 175ms on /v1/complete. Last 7d: uptime 99.94%, p50=88ms, p95=240ms, p99=610ms. Breach: p95 >175ms on 3 days, two of which are business days.
ron: contract triggers credit if p95 > 175ms on more than 1 business day in rolling 7d. We'll need: daily timeseries CSV, top traces for tail requests, autoscale & cache events, and request/token counts during breach windows.
john: legal reminder: use "provisional" wording in any outbound note and include audit sources (CSV + trace ids). Also avoid language that conditions credit on customer actions.
slo-bot: automated: 2026-02-14T08:45Z - p95 exceeded 175ms on 3 days in rolling 7d. Incident ticket CS-7070 created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/CS-7070
lee: ops hypothesis: cache churn plus two short scale-down events during peak. I'll pull cache eviction logs and scaler timeline. Suggest a low-risk canary: enable prefix caching + one prewarmed replica for 24h.
amy: communication plan: 1) one-page customer note explaining findings, 2) mitigation we will try (canary + optional synthetic), 3) provisional credit calc & method, 4) appendix with raw data. Deadline: 48h so CSM can review before renewal call.
ron: credit calc draft: provisional_credit = (breach_days / 7) * monthly_commitment * credit_rate. Need total requests in breach days and avg tokens to compute final numbers. I'll prepare two scenarios: (A) no remediation, (B) remediation reduces breach days -> adjusted credit.
lee: quick ops commands I'll run and attach outputs:
```
redwood metrics export --service inference --route "/v1/complete" --since 7d --agg p50,p95,p99,requests,uptime --by day > bayleaf-metrics.csv
redwood traces list --route "/v1/complete" --filter "latency>300" --limit 15 > bayleaf-traces.ndjson
redwood infra events --since 7d --filter "cache_eviction OR autoscale" > bayleaf-infra.log
```
amy: can we ask Bayleaf for a short synthetic run during the canary window? if they can run 20-30min we might validate warmup and reduce provisional credit. @bayleaf-contact can you confirm?
bayleaf-contact: we can run a 25min synthetic at 03:00 UTC tomorrow. happy to help.
john: legal: we'll review the draft wording once you include CSVs + trace ids. Also include exact breach windows and token counts.
ron: I'll schedule canary toggle at 01:30 UTC (prefix cache + 1 warm replica). will post 6h snapshot and 24h summary. low-risk.
amy: assigning owners: lee (infra traces + canary), ron (metrics export + credit calc scenarios), john (legal wording). I'll consolidate bundle and route to legal for signoff. Any blockers?
lee: none. I'll attach top 10 traces and eviction timeline to CS-7070 after the 6h check.
amy: great. Draft customer note should present provisional credit but say it's subject to final verification and may be adjusted if mitigation proves effective within 48h. keep tone factual.
ron: will upload provisional spreadsheet with placeholders by EOD today.
amy: thanks team. closing loop: if canary + synthetic lower p95 below 175ms within 48h we'll propose a reduced final credit; otherwise proceed with provisional credit and comms. Marking renewal risk as "monitoring" for now and will update renewal tracker. :white_check_mark:
